output.summary: The admitted-patient ED length-of-stay rise is almost entirely boarding (1.4 h to 4.4 h). It began in March, when the hospitalist rounding change pushed medical-ward discharges later. Nurse staffing, ED volume and acuity, and inpatient bed capacity were flat, so they do not explain it. Surgical wards, which did not change rounding, show no discharge shift. The 4 West huddle pilot ran on days set by the rotation schedule before the pilot was designed. On those days it roughly halved boarding, and the comparison days were similar. So extend the huddle to the other medical wards, with weekly tracking. Travel nurses funded by deferring case managers, and pausing the huddle, would both work against the mechanism. The evening bed-cleaning cut remains unmeasured, and the link between boarding and door-to-provider time is confounded by the May triage-provider discontinuation.
